quests.hint: Listen for whether the company reported strong profits or strong growth.
quests.explanation: 'Profits' are the money earned after expenses; 'growth' refers to an increase in size, revenue, or market share. A company can have growth without being profitable, or profits without growth - a key business English distinction.
quests.textToSpeak: The company reported strong profits for the third consecutive year.
quests.correctAnswer: The company reported strong growth for the third consecutive year.

quests.hint: Notice whether inflation is affecting the ability to save or spend.
quests.explanation: Inflation affects both saving and spending, but differently. 'Ability to save' means putting money aside; 'ability to spend' means purchasing power. Both are valid claims, but they describe opposite financial behaviours.
quests.textToSpeak: Rising inflation is affecting people's ability to save money.
quests.correctAnswer: Rising inflation is affecting people's ability to spend money.

quests.hint: Focus on whether small businesses are vital to economic health or growth.
quests.explanation: 'Health of the economy' implies stability and function; 'growth of the economy' implies expansion. Both are valid claims about small businesses. In economic discussions, these two concepts are frequently distinguished.
quests.textToSpeak: Small businesses are vital to the health of the local economy.
quests.correctAnswer: Small businesses are vital to the growth of the local economy.

quests.hint: Listen for how many weeks the art exhibition ran.
quests.explanation: 'Three weeks' and 'two weeks' differ by a week - seemingly small but significant for planning. 'The exhibition attracted thousands of visitors over [time]' uses 'over' to mean 'during a period of'.
quests.textToSpeak: The exhibition attracted thousands of visitors over three weeks.
quests.correctAnswer: The exhibition attracted thousands of visitors over two weeks.

quests.hint: Notice whether young artists or young musicians struggle to earn a living.
quests.explanation: Both artists and musicians face financial challenges in creative careers, but they are different fields. This distinction matters when discussing specific career paths. 'Struggle to earn a living from their work' is a useful phrase.
quests.textToSpeak: Many young artists struggle to earn a living from their work.
quests.correctAnswer: Many young musicians struggle to earn a living from their work.

quests.hint: Focus on whether the film was a commercial failure or success.
quests.explanation: 'Commercial failure' means it made little money; 'commercial success' means it made a lot. Films can receive critical praise either way. 'Critical praise but commercial failure' is a classic critical vs popular distinction in English.
quests.textToSpeak: The film received critical praise but was a commercial failure.
quests.correctAnswer: The film received critical praise and was a commercial success.

quests.hint: Listen for whether researchers developed a vaccine or a treatment.
quests.explanation: A 'vaccine' prevents disease before infection; a 'treatment' manages disease after infection. These are medically very different. In health reporting, confusing prevention with treatment would be a significant error.
quests.textToSpeak: Researchers have developed a new vaccine against the disease.
quests.correctAnswer: Researchers have developed a new treatment for the disease.

quests.hint: Notice whether artificial intelligence or automation is changing work.
quests.explanation: 'Artificial intelligence' (AI) refers to machine learning and smart systems; 'automation' refers to machines performing repetitive tasks. AI is a type of technology; automation is a broader process. Both are transforming work.
quests.textToSpeak: Artificial intelligence is changing the way we work and live.
quests.correctAnswer: Automation is changing the way we work and live.

quests.hint: Pay attention to whether the mission landed on or orbited Mars.
quests.explanation: 'Landed on the surface' means physical contact; 'orbited the surface' means circling around without touching. These are completely different mission achievements - a crucial distinction in space science reporting.
quests.textToSpeak: The space mission successfully landed on the surface of Mars.
quests.correctAnswer: The space mission successfully orbited the surface of Mars.

quests.hint: Listen for by how many seconds the athlete broke the world record.
quests.explanation: 'Two seconds' and 'three seconds' seem small, but in elite athletics they are enormous differences. Precise numbers matter enormously in sports reporting. 'Broke the world record by [amount]' is the standard sports English phrase.
quests.textToSpeak: The athlete broke the world record by two seconds.
quests.correctAnswer: The athlete broke the world record by three seconds.

quests.hint: Notice whether team spirit or training is key to sporting success.
quests.explanation: 'Team spirit' is the collective motivation and unity of a group; 'training' refers to physical and technical preparation. Both contribute to sporting success but represent different aspects - mental vs physical preparation.
quests.textToSpeak: Team spirit and discipline are key to sporting success.
quests.correctAnswer: Training and discipline are key to sporting success.

quests.hint: Focus on whether the match was postponed or cancelled.
quests.explanation: 'Postponed' means rescheduled to a later date; 'cancelled' means permanently called off. This is a crucial distinction in sports - a postponed match will still be played; a cancelled one will not.
quests.textToSpeak: The match was postponed due to bad weather conditions.
quests.correctAnswer: The match was cancelled due to bad weather conditions.

quests.hint: Listen for whether body language or non-verbal language is mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Body language' includes gestures, posture, and facial expressions; 'non-verbal language' is the broader category including body language, tone of voice, and eye contact. Body language is a type of non-verbal communication.
quests.textToSpeak: Body language accounts for a large part of human communication.
quests.correctAnswer: Non-verbal language accounts for a large part of human communication.

quests.hint: Notice whether she expressed herself clearly or confidently.
quests.explanation: 'Clearly' means in an understandable way; 'confidently' means without hesitation or fear. You can speak clearly without being confident, or be confident without being clear. These adverbs describe different qualities of communication.
quests.textToSpeak: She expressed herself clearly despite the language barrier.
quests.correctAnswer: She expressed herself confidently despite the language barrier.

quests.hint: Focus on whether listening well is as important as speaking or writing.
quests.explanation: 'Speaking' and 'writing' are both productive skills - you produce language output. Listening is often undervalued compared to speaking in particular. 'Just as important as' is a structure for arguing equal importance.
quests.textToSpeak: The ability to listen well is just as important as speaking.
quests.correctAnswer: The ability to listen well is just as important as writing.

quests.hint: Listen for whether citizens have the right to vote or participate.
quests.explanation: 'Vote' is a specific act in an election; 'participate' is broader, including campaigning, running for office, and civic engagement. Both are democratic rights, but 'participate' encompasses more activities.
quests.textToSpeak: Citizens have the right to vote in free and fair elections.
quests.correctAnswer: Citizens have the right to participate in free and fair elections.

quests.hint: Notice whether the policy divided experts or politicians and the public.
quests.explanation: 'Experts' are specialists in a field; 'politicians' are elected representatives. Both groups may have divided opinions, but these represent very different sources of disagreement - technical versus political.
quests.textToSpeak: The policy has divided opinion among experts and the public.
quests.correctAnswer: The policy has divided opinion among politicians and the public.

quests.hint: Focus on whether transparency or accountability builds trust in government.
quests.explanation: 'Transparency' means being open about decisions and information; 'accountability' means being answerable for actions and outcomes. Both are democratic values but with different emphases. Very common vocabulary in political discourse.
quests.textToSpeak: Greater transparency in government builds trust among citizens.
quests.correctAnswer: Greater accountability in government builds trust among citizens.

quests.hint: Listen for whether people move abroad for better opportunities or better conditions.
quests.explanation: 'Opportunities' refers to chances for advancement (jobs, education); 'conditions' refers to quality of life (safety, healthcare, environment). Both motivate migration but represent different priorities.
quests.textToSpeak: Many people move abroad in search of better opportunities.
quests.correctAnswer: Many people move abroad in search of better conditions.

quests.hint: Notice whether cultural or national identity is linked to wellbeing.
quests.explanation: 'Cultural identity' relates to shared customs, language, and traditions; 'national identity' relates to citizenship and belonging to a country. They often overlap but are conceptually distinct - important in multicultural discussions.
quests.textToSpeak: Cultural identity is an important part of personal wellbeing.
quests.correctAnswer: National identity is an important part of personal wellbeing.

quests.hint: Pay attention to whether migration is enriched through diversity and perspectives or shared experiences.
quests.explanation: 'New perspectives' implies fresh ways of seeing things; 'shared experiences' implies common understanding through joint events. Both enrich societies, but perspectives suggest intellectual diversity while experiences suggest social bonds.
quests.textToSpeak: Migration has enriched societies through diversity and new perspectives.
quests.correctAnswer: Migration has enriched societies through diversity and shared experiences.

quests.hint: Listen for whether goals keep you focused or organised.
quests.explanation: 'Focused' means concentrating on what matters; 'organised' means having a system for managing tasks. Setting goals contributes to both, but they describe different cognitive benefits. 'Helps you stay + adjective' is a natural structure.
quests.textToSpeak: Setting clear goals helps you stay focused and motivated.
quests.correctAnswer: Setting clear goals helps you stay organised and motivated.

quests.hint: Notice whether she took a course to improve public speaking or presentation skills.
quests.explanation: 'Public speaking' is the act of speaking to an audience; 'presentation skills' is broader, covering visual aids, structure, and delivery. A presentation course might cover both, but the terms differ in scope.
quests.textToSpeak: She took a course to improve her public speaking skills.
quests.correctAnswer: She took a course to improve her presentation skills.

quests.hint: Focus on whether failure or mistakes are the best teacher.
quests.explanation: 'Failure' and 'mistakes' are related but different - failure is a broader outcome; mistakes are specific errors. Both teach valuable lessons. 'X is often the best teacher for long-term Y' is a motivational English structure.
quests.textToSpeak: Failure is often the best teacher for long-term success.
quests.correctAnswer: Mistakes are often the best teacher for long-term success.

quests.hint: Listen for whether property or rental prices have risen dramatically.
quests.explanation: 'Property prices' refer to the cost of buying a home; 'rental prices' refer to monthly costs for renting. Both have risen in many cities, but they affect different groups - buyers vs renters. An important housing vocabulary distinction.
quests.textToSpeak: Property prices in major cities have risen dramatically in recent years.
quests.correctAnswer: Rental prices in major cities have risen dramatically in recent years.

quests.hint: Notice whether urban regeneration or urban planning is mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Urban regeneration' means revitalising existing areas; 'urban planning' means designing and organising new or existing city spaces. Regeneration is reactive (fixing problems); planning is proactive (designing for the future).
quests.textToSpeak: Urban regeneration projects can transform neglected areas.
quests.correctAnswer: Urban planning projects can transform neglected areas.

quests.hint: Focus on whether she chose a shared or smaller house.
quests.explanation: 'Shared house' means living with other people; 'smaller house' means a more compact home. Both reduce costs but through different means. 'She chose to live in a...' is a natural structure for explaining housing decisions.
quests.textToSpeak: She chose to live in a shared house to reduce her costs.
quests.correctAnswer: She chose to live in a smaller house to reduce her costs.

quests.hint: Listen for whether communication should be honest or respectful.
quests.explanation: 'Honest' and 'respectful' are both qualities of good communication, but sometimes in tension - honesty can be disrespectful; respect can require softening the truth. 'Open and honest' vs 'open and respectful' suggest different priorities.
quests.textToSpeak: Open and honest communication is the foundation of any relationship.
quests.correctAnswer: Open and respectful communication is the foundation of any relationship.

quests.hint: Notice whether she found it hard to express her feelings or discuss her problems.
quests.explanation: 'Express feelings' relates to emotional communication; 'discuss problems' relates to practical communication. Both are relationship communication skills, but emotional expression and problem-solving require different skills.
quests.textToSpeak: She found it difficult to express her feelings to her partner.
quests.correctAnswer: She found it difficult to discuss her problems with her partner.

quests.hint: Pay attention to whether understanding or accepting differences strengthens relationships.
quests.explanation: 'Understanding differences' means intellectually grasping them; 'accepting differences' means emotionally and practically embracing them. Acceptance goes further than understanding - you can understand something you don't accept.
quests.textToSpeak: Understanding each other's differences leads to stronger relationships.
quests.correctAnswer: Accepting each other's differences leads to stronger relationships.
